1  THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, R/W SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C. PRAYING TO a) QUASH THE ORDER TITLED AS 'ORDER ON APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 258 CR.P.C.'
PASSED BY THE LD. MAGISTRATE, ADDITIONAL J.J.BOARD,
KALABURAGI, DATED 17-07-2023 IN J.C.NO.52 OF 2020 FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 143, 147, 148,
302, 341, 427, 448, 504, 506(2) AND 120(B) READ WITH SECTION 149 OF IPC, WHICH IS AT PAGE 56-58 OF THE PETITION AT ANNEXURE-C, B) TO DIRECT THE ADDITIONAL J.
J. BOARD, KALABURAGI TO PROCEED AGAINST THIS PETITIONER IN J.C.NO.52/2020 AS PER THE PROVISIONS OF JUVENILE JUSTICE (CARE AND PROTECTION OF CHILDREN)
ACT, 2015, C) TO QUASH FURTHER PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THIS PETITIONER IN S.C.NO.103/2020 PENDING BEFORE III ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, KALABURAGI,
D)

TO DIRECT THE STATE OF KARNATAKA TO RELEASE THE PETITIONER/CCL CURRENTLY HELD AT GULBARGA CENTRAL PRISON, KALABURAGI BY HOLDING HIS J.C PERIOD AS 'SENTENCE ALREADY UNDERGONE' IN TERMS OF S.18 OF THE JJ ACT AND E) TO PASS SUCH OTHER ORDERS AS THIS HON'BLE COURT DEEMS FIT AND PROPER IN THE LIGHT OF FACTS AND CIRCUMSTANCES NARRATED ABOVE.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224  WP No. 200172 of 2024  ORDER

This petition has been filed under Articles 226 and 227 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking writ of certiorari to quash the order dated 17.07.2023 by the Juvenile Justice Board (for short 'JJB') in J.C.No.52/2020, which is at Annexure-C.
02.

The brief facts germane are that a case was registered in the Nelogi Police Station, Jewargi Circle, Kalarburagi District, in Crime No.70/2020, who after the investigation filed a charge-sheet against the accuse Nos.1 to 6, wherein the present petitioner was shown as accused No.4, for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 148, 302, 341, 427, 448, 504 and 506(2) and 120(B)
read with Section 149 of IPC.

Thereafter, the accused Nos.1 to 6 including the petitioner had approached the Ld. Prl. Sessions Judge Kalaburagi in Crl.Misc.No.1027/2020 seeking regular bail,
which came to be allowed by order dated 01.10.2020.

2 03.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Against the said order, the de-facto complainant had approached this Court in Crl.P.No.200968/2020 seeking cancellation of the bail.
The said petition came to be allowed on 25.02.2021.

Consequently, the petitioner herein / the accused No.4 surrendered before the Sessions Court and he was remanded to judicial custody on 26.02.2021.
04.

In the meanwhile, the Investigating Officer had also filed a charge-sheet against the petitioner herein before the JJB at Kalabuagi on 24.09.2020 and the JJB took cognizance of the case and summoned the petitioner to appear.
Thereafter, it had, by an order dated 22.03.2021, when the petitioner had appeared before it had granted the bail.

Thereafter, the petitioner did not appear and NBW were issued to the petitioner by the JJB and ultimately, it was informed to the JJB that the petitioner (who is referred to as CCL by the JJB) was also charge-sheeted and the matter is pending before the III Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi in NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224 S.C.103/2020.

entities.text: III Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ultimately, by an order dated 10.07.2023 the further proceedings before the JJB came to closed under Section 258 of Cr.P.C.
The said order is now under challenge in this writ petition.

05. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the Investigating Officer had filed the charge- sheet against the petitioner before the JJB as well as before the Magistrate (Later the case was committed to the Sessions Court), which is illegal.
He submits that the alleged incident had taken place on 09.05.2020, on which date, the petitioner was a minor.
It is contended that the petitioner was born on 09.08.2002 and as such the Investigating Officer could not have charge-sheeted the petitioner before the regular Court by showing his age as 19 years.
The learned Magistrate and the Sessions Court believed the age to be 19 years and proceeded with the matter.

When the bail granted to the petitioner by Sessions Court is challenged before this Court in Crl.P.No.200968/2020, this Court also went under the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224 premise that the petitioner is aged 19 years.
The question of the age of the petitioner was not raised and not considered by this Court.
06. Therefore, he submits that, when the age of the petitioner was less than 18 years, he should have been tried by the JJB.

Due to the act of the Investigating Officer, the petitioner was in custody from 10.05.2020 when he was arrested, till 01.10.2020 when he was granted bail by the Sessions Court and then from 26.02.2021 when he surrendered due to cancellation of bail, till today.
Therefore, it is submitted that being a Juvenile he could not have been tried by the Sessions Court, and the JJB fell in error in closing the further proceedings.
Therefore, he seeks quashing of the entire proceedings as against the petitioner.

07. The learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent for the State would submit that the Investigating Officer could not have filed charge- sheet before the regular court and also the JJB.

When the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224 matter is heard, it was submitted that the learned III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi has directed the petitioner to be produced before the JJB and has also ordered that the Commissioner of Police Kalaburagi and S.P. concerned, has to take necessary action against the Investigating Officer, who has submitted false information before the Courts of law.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, she submits that the JJB would commence the proceedings against the petitioner.

She also submitted that the maximum punishment that could be awarded by the JJB has Malappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38287311/
3 been undergone by the petitioner by remaining in custody.

entities.text: JJB has Malappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, she submitted that the suitable orders may be passed.

08. It is evident from the records that though the Investigating Officer had filed the charge-sheet before the JJB showing the petitioner as minor, such information was not given the regular court and the charge-shet nowhere mentioned that the petitioner was being prosecuted before the JJB.
Now, the Sessions Court, acting on the application NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224 filed by the LADC counsel, sent the petitioner to the JJB.
It also came to the conclusion that the petitioner should have been tried by the JJB as per the charge-sheet of the Investigating Officer.
09. Thus, it is evident that the petitioner has spent 03 years 05 months in custody.
In fact the petitioner should have been tried by the JJB.
The question of juvenility can be raised at any point of time.
This Court in the case of Shrishail vs. State of Karnataka (Crl.A.No.200241/2023 dated 21.12.2023) had an occasion to deal with such circumstances.

entities.text: Shrishail vs. State of Karnataka (Crl.A.No.200241/2023 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A minor was prosecuted before a regular court and also was convicted.
In appeal Juvenility was established.

By relying on the judgment in the case of Raju vs. State of Haryana1, held that the accused need not face the trial afresh by JJB, since he has already spent the maximum period for which a juvenile may be sent to a special home.

Para No.27 of the judgment of the Apex Court reads as below:-
(2019) 14 SCC 401 NC: 2024:KHC-K:2224 "27.
The criminal appeal hereby stands allowed and the order of the High Court affirming the conviction and sentence of the appellant under Section 376 (2) (g) IPC is set-aside.

Seeing that the appellant has already spent 6 years in imprisonment, whereas the maximum period for which a juvenile may be sent to a special home is only 3 years as per Section 15 (1) (g) of the 2000 Act, and since the appellant has already been enlarged on bail by virtue of the order of the Court dated 09.05.2014, he need not be taken into custody.
His bail bonds stand discharged and all proceedings against him, so far as they relate to the present case, stand terminated."
It is also relevant to note that the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Rishipal Singh Solanki vs. State of U.P.2, deals with the manner in which a juvenility has to be considered.

entities.text: Rishipal Singh Solanki vs. State of U.P.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, it is not in dispute that the petitioner was a minor.
The Investigating Officer had filed a charge-sheet before the JJB stating that he was a minor.
The petitioner has also produced the school transfer certificate which shows that he was born on 09.08.2002.
Therefore, the fact that the petitioner was a minor is not in dispute.

Hence, even if the petitioner is sent to face the trial before the JJB it would be a futile exercise since he has already spent the maximum punishment which could have been imposed by the JJB by sending him to special home for juveniles.

Therefore, the relief claimed by the petitioner seeking quashment of the entire proceedings before the JJB arising out of the Crime No.70/2020 of Nilogi P.S., Jewargi Circle, Kalaburagi District, is liable to be allowed.

Hence, the following; (2022) 8 SCC 602 Malappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38287311/

sentences.text: The writ petition is allowed.
II. The proceedings before the JJB arising out of the Crime No.70/2020 of Nelogi P.S., Jewargi Circle Kalaburagi City, so far as it pertains to petitioner, is quashed.
III. The petitioner is ordered to be set as liberty if he is not required in other cases.

IV. The Police Commissioner / S.P. shall take note of the order passed by the learned III Addl.
District and Sessions Court at Kalaburagi in S.C.No.103/2020 and take appropriate action in the matter.
